topic: Distance, Displacement, Speed, Velocity, and Acceleration
key_concepts: Distance is the length of the path traveled
Displacement is the final position relative to the initial position with direction
Distance is a scalar quantity with magnitude only
Displacement is a vector quantity with magnitude and direction
Displacement can be positive, negative, or zero depending on direction relative to the ini
Speed is the total distance traveled per unit time and is a scalar quantity
Velocity is displacement per unit time and is a vector quantity
Speed and velocity can be calculated using the formula v = d/t
Uniform motion covers equal distances in equal time intervals
Non-uniform motion covers unequal distances in equal time intervals
Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the change in time
An object accelerates when its velocity changes
